models.long_text: Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct (Q4_K_M GGUF, Apache-2.0) via llama.cpp llama-server

risks: CoreWeave relies on Microsoft for 62% of its revenue.
CoreWeave entered into a master services agreement with OpenAI for up to $11.9 billion.
CoreWeave faces risks from potential liabilities from acquired companies and changing regulations.
CoreWeave's bylaws specify exclusive forums for certain legal actions.
CoreWeave's multi-class stock structure concentrates voting power with Co-Founders.

growth_drivers: Revenue increased by $1.4 billion, or 112%, in the three months ended June 30, 2026, due to increased demand from both existing and new customers.
CoreWeave provides developer tools and integrations for building and deploying AI models and agents.
risks: The company expects to continue incurring additional expenses due to projected future growth.

growth_drivers: CoreWeave delivers a comprehensive, tightly integrated platform of advanced infrastructure and proprietary software for AI systems.
Revenue increased by $3.2 billion, or 168%, due to higher demand from both existing and new customers.
CoreWeave had $60.7 billion of remaining performance obligations as of December 31, 2025.
CoreWeave expects increasing adoption of AI globally, leading to new industries and use cases that will drive demand for its cloud platform.
risks: Interest expense increased significantly due to higher borrowing levels, impacting cash flow.
We expect our cost of revenue to increase in absolute dollar terms as we grow our platform and customer base.

growth_drivers: Caterpillar is deploying NVIDIA's Vera Rubin platform to support physical AI training and inference at industrial scale.
CoreWeave surpassed 1 billion model training runs tracked on its platform.
CoreWeave became the first cloud provider to bring up and validate NVIDIA's Vera Rubin NVL72.
CoreWeave expects demand to meaningfully exceed supply for years, driving growth.
Q2 was an exceptional quarter marked by intense customer demand and significant ramp of active capacity.
risks: CoreWeave expects 2026 CapEx in the range of $35 billion to $39 billion.

growth_drivers: CoreWeave's managed inference product grew from $1 million to $100 million in a single quarter.
CoreWeave can sell GPUs from 2020 in contracts until 2029, indicating strong demand for older infrastructure.
CoreWeave can now offer compute on 2 or 3 year contracts, opening up new markets.
CoreWeave's infrastructure is more valuable to customers, leading to higher margins.
risks: CoreWeave has contracted 4.2 gigawatts and has options for another 1.5 gigawatts, putting them close to 6 gigawatts by mid-2026.
